A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M2N2 research work. Their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including v2's added supplementary Sections 6–14; v1 ends with its references.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation results on four datasets, component ablations, parameter sensitivity experiments and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds backbone comparisons, medical-image evaluations and supplementary quantitative and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adds SD1.1 and DINOv2 ViT-B variants. The ViT adaptation removes the CLS token and uses the last attention layer (Section 13). The original SD2 Markov-map, flood-fill and truncated-nearest-neighbor procedure remains unchanged; the new flood-fill pseudocode documents that existing procedure.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands beyond the retained GrabCut, Berkeley, SBD and DAVIS datasets to medical images from BraTS and OAIZIB. This introduces a substantially different domain and tests applicability beyond natural images.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds reported comparisons with FocalClick, InterFormer-Tiny and OIS, with OIS represented only on DAVIS NoC90. The existing supervised and unsupervised comparators remain, so the principal unsupervised comparison is preserved.

E3.justification: The original dataset splits, simulated click policy, 20-click limit and NoC85/NoC90 protocol remain unchanged. Added evaluations introduce medical IoU after 10 clicks, mIoU-versus-click curves and alternative backbone/resolution settings. Section 8 newly documents baseline temperatures without establishing that the original comparisons were rerun or retuned.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the original ablations, v2 adds backbone-resolution sensitivity, medical-domain testing, an IPF/Markov-chain visualization, click-count distributions, 42 SBD failure cases and detailed score-function case studies. These substantially expand evidence about mechanisms, parameter sensitivity and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new click-count histograms describe variation across instances rather than uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in Tables 1–3 are retained, while v2 adds comparator and backbone scores, interaction curves and failure examples. New medical IoUs are 70% versus SimpleClick's 87% on BraTS and 66% versus 76% on OAIZIB after 10 clicks. Reported click time changes from 900 ms to 0.6 seconds, without explaining the cause.

T1.justification: Supplementary Section 6 adds a derivation, Equations 12–18, establishing the equivalence of temperature adjustment through log probabilities and direct logit scaling. The existing Markov-chain reasoning and main method equations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a novel attention-based, unsupervised, training-free interactive segmentation framework, improved semantic maps and superiority over trained unsupervised methods on three of the four original benchmarks. Mentioning multiple-backbone experiments expands supporting evidence without redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly acknowledges medical-domain bias, proposes SBD annotation-boundary mismatch and enclosed background regions as failure explanations, and interprets backbone-resolution saturation as a reason to choose SD2. These substantially extend the earlier discussion of overlapping objects, obstructions and fine structures.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, priority-queue flood-fill pseudocode and CPU execution information. It also discloses Attention-NN's temperature of 10, KL-NN's temperature of 2 and clipping range, plus detailed backbone extraction and resolution choices. These materially improve reproducibility without demonstrating changes to the original implementation.

R1.justification: The supervised related-work discussion adopts a dense-versus-sparse prompt-fusion taxonomy. References add InterFormer, OIS, DINOv2 and supporting datasets, while Conditional Diffusion and EdgeFlow citations disappear. The central positioning relative to DiffSeg and unsupervised interactive segmentation remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most exposition remain intact. Local revisions clarify the interaction loop, condense supervised related work, rewrite the qualitative-limitations discussion, standardize Markov-map notation and update the affiliation. Supplementary Sections 6–14 organize the additional material.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 3, adds another failure-case column to Figure 5, and introduces Algorithm 1 and Figures 6–13. The new diagrams, curves, histograms and extensive qualitative panels substantially expand the visual presentation; the earlier principal framework figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The flood-fill pseudocode and baseline settings improve reproducibility, while medical tests and SBD failure analysis clarify limitations missing from v1. These gains are tempered by sparse medical protocol details and an unexplained mismatch between Figure 13's ViT-B DAVIS curve and Table 3 at the stated resolution. Overall, v2 is more informative, with remaining weaknesses in the added evidence.
